To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the expression of the natural antisense RNA of cTn I is cell type-specific in the neonatal heart.
natural antisense RNA transcripts of cTN I are co-expressed with the corresponding sense RNA in NCM and in NCF, but that the expression pattern varies in both cell types.
natural antisense RNA of cTnT is co-expressed with the sense RNA in both cell types and that the relative expression of the antisense transcript varies in different cell types.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and analysis of natural antisense transcripts in the rat heart.
a quantitative analysis of antisense RNA expression in the neonatal heart.
the analysis of antisense RNA transcription in the human and rat heart.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the antisense RNA expression pattern in a tissue is dependent on the cell type.
the expression of the antisense and sense cTnI RNAs is cell type-specific and the antisense RNA is expressed in a higher relative amount in cardiac fibroblats than in cardiomyocytes.
the expression of natural antisense cTnI transcripts is not only restricted to a certain developmental stage, but that also the cell type-specific expression pattern is of importance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the expression pattern of sense and antisence RNA of cTnC can vary between different tissues as well as between different cell types of one tissue.
the expression of natural occurring antisense RNA is not only tissue specific but also cell type specific.
antisense and sense RNAs of cTnT and cTnI can be detected in both cell types and that the relative amount of natural antisense cTnI is higher in NCF than in NCM.
The main takeaway from our work is that
antisense RNA is expressed in different cell types and that the expression pattern can vary.
antisense RNA can be detected in a cell type-specific manner.
antisense transcripts are co-expressing with the corresponding sense transcripts in different cell types.
